title: China’s Arctic Comeback
author: Marc Lanteigne
text:
China’s Yellow River facility in Svalbard – before the stone lions were ordered to be removed.
Credit: Marc Lanteigne
It has been almost a decade now since Beijing announced its revised Arctic strategy, particularly focused on the development of the Polar Silk Road (PSR), a segment of the Belt and Road Initiative originally conceived as an emerging “blue economic channel” connecting Europe with Northeast Asia via the Northern Sea Route. The PSR would later be incorporated into Beijing’s 2018 governmental White Paper on the Arctic, as China sought to “understand, protect, develop, and participate in the governance” of the far north, while positioning itself as a “near-Arctic state” and regional stakeholder. While maintaining emphasis on Arctic scientific cooperation, China began to exhibit stronger interests in regional economic, and to a degree strategic, initiatives in the years following the publication of the White Paper.[...]
